title: Challenging an anxious or self-critical thought
content: A CBT thought record helps slow down a distressing thought and examine it: name the situation, the automatic thought, the feeling it created, the evidence for and against it, and a more balanced thought.
source: Cognitive behavioral therapy — thought record (standard clinical exercise)
license: Concept — public domain; exercise scaffold, no copyrighted worksheet copied

title: Unsent letter
content: Writing an unsent letter lets a person say what is hard to say aloud — to someone they miss, someone who hurt them, or their past self — with no consequences.

metadata.prompt: Write a letter you will never send to the person on your mind. Say everything you haven't been able to say.

title: Values reflection (ACT)
content: An ACT values exercise: reflect on the kind of person you want to be in a hard area of life, and one small action that moves you toward it — even while difficult feelings are present.
source: Acceptance and commitment therapy — values clarification (standard clinical exercise)

metadata.prompt: What matters most to you in the area of life that feels hardest right now, and what is one small step that would honor it?

title: Worry postponement
content: Worry time is a CBT technique: instead of fighting worries all day, note them down and set aside a short, scheduled time later to attend to them, freeing attention in the meantime.
source: Cognitive behavioral therapy — stimulus control for worry (standard clinical exercise)

metadata.prompt: List the worries on your mind right now. We'll set them aside together for a scheduled worry time.
